deep.reconstruction:
PROBLEM (Aufgabe). A spherical triangle ABC is given. It is to be cut into four parts of equal area by the arcs GE, GF, EF, where G lies on AB, E on BC and F on CA. Standard notation is used: a = BC, b = CA, c = AB.

UNKNOWNS. The transcription reads 'GF = lambda'. The formulas only make sense if lambda = CF (the C-corner triangle has sides CE = a - theta and CF = lambda, and the A-corner triangle has AF = b - lambda). So the unknowns are lambda = CF, theta = EB, mu = AG.

AREA CONDITION. Write E = A + B + C - 180 deg for the spherical excess of ABC, and set eps = E/8. If the three corner triangles CEF, BGE and AGF each have excess E/4, then the middle triangle GEF also has E/4. So the problem reduces to three corner conditions in three unknowns.

TOOL. For a spherical triangle with sides x, y enclosing angle C, its excess E' satisfies
  cot(E'/2) = (cot(x/2) cot(y/2) + cos C) / sin C.
This is the half-excess formula in two sides and the included angle (equivalently tan(E'/2) = t sin C / (1 + t cos C), with t = tan(x/2) tan(y/2)). With E'/2 = E/8 = eps this gives the page's three equations:
  [cot(lambda/2) cot((a-theta)/2) + cos C] / sin C = cot eps
  [cot(theta/2) cot((c-mu)/2) + cos B] / sin B = cot eps
  [cot(mu/2) cot((b-lambda)/2) + cos A] / sin A = cot eps

STEP (psi). Use cot(eps) sin C - cos C = sin(C - eps) / sin(eps). This gives:
  cot(lambda/2) cot((a-theta)/2) = sin(C-eps)/sin eps
  cot(theta/2) cot((c-mu)/2) = sin(B-eps)/sin eps
  cot(mu/2) cot((b-lambda)/2) = sin(A-eps)/sin eps

ELIMINATION. The page claims that x = tan(mu/2) satisfies
  x^2 - x [(t-p) tan(c/2) + q - r] / (t + q tan(c/2)) + (r tan(c/2) - p) / (t + q tan(c/2)) = 0,
with
  p = sin^2 eps cot(a/2) cot(b/2) [alpha + tan(a/2) tan(b/2)]
  t = sin(B-eps) sin(A-eps) [alpha - cot(a/2) cot(b/2)]
  q = sin eps sin(A-eps) [alpha + cot(b/2) tan(a/2)]
  r = sin eps sin(B-eps) [alpha - cot(a/2) tan(b/2)]
Here alpha = sin(C-eps)/sin eps. Then theta and lambda follow from (psi).

MY ELIMINATION (mine, for comparison). Put Ta = tan(a/2), Tb = tan(b/2), Tc = tan(c/2), alpha as above, beta = sin(B-eps)/sin eps, gamma = sin(A-eps)/sin eps, u = tan(lambda/2), v = tan(theta/2).
- From (psi)3: u = (gamma x Tb - 1) / (Tb + gamma x).
- From (psi)1: v = (alpha u Ta - 1) / (alpha u + Ta).
- From (psi)2: v = (1 + Tc x) / (beta (Tc - x)).
Equating the two expressions for v gives
  (gamma Tc K3 + beta gamma K1) x^2 + (gamma K3 + Tc K4 - beta gamma Tc K1 - beta K2) x + (K4 + beta Tc K2) = 0,
where K1 = alpha Ta Tb - 1, K2 = alpha Ta + Tb, K3 = alpha Tb + Ta, K4 = Ta Tb - alpha.
The shape is the same as the page's (t + q Tc) x^2 ... form. In normalized form one would need:
  t ~ beta gamma (alpha - cot(a/2) cot(b/2)), which agrees with the page;
  q ~ gamma (alpha cot(a/2) + cot(b/2)) and r ~ beta (alpha cot(b/2) + cot(a/2)), which differ from the page by a factor and/or a sign;
  p ~ alpha cot(a/2) cot(b/2) - 1;
  and the linear coefficient's signs differ.
So the method (eliminate theta and lambda to get a quadratic in tan(mu/2)) is right, but the coefficients as written could not be confirmed. This should be checked by computer.

REMARK (mine). The problem is not always solvable. For the octant triangle (A = B = C = 90 deg, a = b = c = 90 deg) the conditions become tan(x/2) tan(y/2) = tan(11.25 deg) at each corner. Multiplying the three conditions and using max tan(x/2) tan((90-x)/2) = tan^2(22.5 deg) ≈ 0.172 gives a contradiction (0.172^3 ≈ 0.005 < tan^3(11.25 deg) ≈ 0.0079). In such cases the quadratic has no admissible real root; the page does not discuss this.

The neat, uniform hand and the textbook 'Aufgabe/Aufloesung' format suggest this may be a pupil's or correspondent's submission kept among Gauss's papers rather than Gauss's own working.
errors: The definition 'GF = lambda' (as transcribed) is inconsistent with the formulas; lambda must be CF (= FC).
The text says cot(mu/2) is determined by the quadratic, but the quadratic is written in tan(mu/2). Minor inconsistency; either variable is equivalent.

An independent elimination of (psi) gives a quadratic in tan(mu/2) whose t-coefficient matches the page, but whose p, q, r and linear-term signs do not match the page's definitions as transcribed. Likely slips (missing factors cot(a/2) in q and cot(b/2) in r, sign errors) in the original or the transcription; to be checked by CAS.
No discussion of existence/admissibility: e.g. for the trirectangular triangle no real configuration exists, so the quadratic can have no admissible root.

results.usually_credited_to: 18th c. (Euler/Lexell circle of results on spherical excess); standard in 19th-c. textbooks

deep.surprise_reason: A routine exercise in spherical trigonometry using the standard two-sides-and-included-angle excess formula plus algebraic elimination. Its coefficients also appear to contain slips, and the hand may not be Gauss's own.
